findings.description: storage_encrypted = false means the RDS MySQL storage, snapshots and automated backups hold application data in cleartext with no KMS protection.

publicly_accessible = true gives the MySQL instance an internet-routable endpoint (also exported through the catalog_db_endpoint output), exposing the database tier to untrusted networks and leaving only security group rules and a static master password as controls.

The master username is hard-coded as the predictable 'admin' and the password comes from var.password, which is stored in plaintext in Terraform state and re-used verbatim in EC2 user_data instead of AWS Secrets Manager or manage_master_user_password.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced for DB connections
findings.description: Neither the attached parameter group nor the option group enforces encrypted client connections (e.g. require_secure_transport), and the application connects via mysqli_connect with no SSL options, so credentials and query data can traverse the network in cleartext.

The user_data script writes the RDS master username and password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data is readable from the instance metadata service by any local process or SSRF-capable web app, and is also visible in Terraform state and the EC2 console, leaking database master credentials.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains available on an internet-facing PHP web server. A single SSRF yields both the credential-bearing user_data and the highly privileged instance profile credentials.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is declared, so the instance volume that stores the plaintext database credential file is likely unencrypted at rest (unless account-level default EBS encryption is enabled).

The bootstrap installs httpd with no TLS configuration and the instance is published via a public DNS output, so the form that submits employee name and address data is served and submitted over unencrypted HTTP.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role attached to the internet-reachable web server. Compromise of the PHP application (or SSRF via IMDSv1) yields near-administrative control of all S3 data, EC2 infrastructure and RDS instances, including privilege-escalation paths such as launching instances with other roles.

MySQL/3306 ingress is permitted from the entire VPC CIDR rather than being scoped to the application server's security group, so any workload in the VPC can reach the database; this is compounded by publicly_accessible = true on the instance.
The database security group allows all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unconstrained data exfiltration and command-and-control path from the database tier.
